questions.q: What is the concrete risk of a Glue job role with "Action": "s3:*", "Resource": "*"?
options: A bug or compromised dependency in that job gains read/write/delete access to every bucket in the account, not just the one it was meant to touch
The policy simply won't work and the job will fail immediately
AWS blocks wildcard policies automatically, so there is no real risk
It only affects billing, not security
questions.explain: A wildcard Action/Resource policy works everywhere, which means any bug or compromise in that job's code inherits access to the entire account's S3 resources, not a scoped subset.

questions.q: What does 'least privilege' mean in the context of IAM roles for pipelines?
options: Granting a role exactly the access its job requires, and nothing more
Giving every role administrator access for simplicity
Only applying restrictions to human IAM users, never to service roles
Rotating credentials once a year regardless of exposure
questions.explain: Least privilege means scoping a role's permissions tightly to what its actual job requires — no broader Action or Resource grants than necessary.

questions.q: What does IAM Access Analyzer do?
options: Scans resource-based policies for access unintentionally granted to external accounts or public principals
Automatically rewrites overly broad policies to be scoped correctly
Encrypts all S3 objects in the account
Replaces the need for trust policies on IAM roles
questions.explain: IAM Access Analyzer scans resource-based policies (like bucket policies and role trust policies) and flags any that grant access to entities outside your account or intended zone of trust.

questions.q: For human operators, what does this lesson recommend instead of long-lived IAM user credentials?
options: IAM Identity Center, providing federated, temporary access
Sharing a single root account password among the team
Storing access keys in a shared spreadsheet
Embedding access keys directly in application code
questions.explain: IAM Identity Center provides federated, temporary access for human operators, serving the same purpose for people that roles serve for services — avoiding standing long-lived credentials.

questions.q: For a Glue job that only needs to read from raw/ and write to curated/, what is the scoped policy approach this lesson recommends over a wildcard?
options: Separate statements granting s3:GetObject on the raw/* ARN and s3:GetObject/s3:PutObject on the curated/* ARN specifically
One statement granting s3:* on the entire account with no Resource restriction
Denying all S3 access and relying solely on public bucket access
Granting IAM administrator access to the Glue service role
questions.explain: Scoping both the Action list and the Resource ARNs to exactly the prefixes and operations the job needs contains the blast radius of any bug or compromise to just those prefixes.
